short_description: BGP Route Flapping Causing Intermittent Packet Drops on Secondary WAN Link
description: Network monitoring alerted on frequent BGP state changes (Established to Active/Idle) on edge router rtr-core-dc2 connecting to ISP-2. Traffic across the secondary WAN circuit is dropping 28% of packets every 6-8 minutes, causing latency spikes in inter-DC replication.
resolution: The incident was diagnosed by analyzing BGP session logs and executing 'show ip bgp summary' on rtr-core-dc2, which revealed frequent hold-timer expirations from ISP-2. Packet capture with tcpdump on interface TenGigE0/0/1 identified asymmetrical Path MTU discovery issues causing TCP RST packets. The team aligned the BGP keepalive and hold timers to 30s/90s, configured 'ip tcp mss-adjust 1400' on the WAN sub-interface, and coordinated with ISP-2 to stabilize route dampening. Packet loss dropped to 0% and BGP neighbor session remained stable.
ground_truth: The root cause was aggressive BGP hold-timer mismatch and MTU black-holing on the secondary ISP link. The issue was resolved by aligning the BGP keepalive/hold timers to 30s/90s on rtr-core-dc2, configuring path MTU discovery, and clamping TCP MSS to 1400 on the transit interface.

short_description: Cannot access internal inventory portal from branch office
description: Staff at the Seattle branch office report that the internal inventory management tool is not loading at all today. Browser says connection timed out. Other websites like Google work fine.
resolution: Initial triage checked the site-to-site IPsec VPN tunnel between the Seattle branch firewall and central datacenter. Running 'show crypto ipsec sa' revealed that Phase 2 Security Associations (SAs) were expired and failing rekeying negotiations. The diagnostic command 'show log crypto' indicated a lifetime parameter mismatch in the IKEv2 transform set. The network engineer cleared the stale crypto sessions using 'clear crypto ipsec sa', synchronized the Phase 2 lifetime to 28800 seconds on the branch Fortinet gateway, and confirmed successful bidirectional ICMP ping to the inventory server at 10.20.14.50.
ground_truth: The root cause was an expired IPsec phase-2 Security Association (SA) lifetime configuration on the Seattle branch gateway router, preventing renegotiation with the central VPN concentrator. Resolved by clearing stale SAs with 'clear crypto ipsec sa', updating the IKEv2 proposal lifetimes to match the central profile, and verifying tunnel stability.

short_description: Internal DNS Resolution Failure for Payment Gateway Microservices
description: Payment processing pods in Kubernetes cluster prod-east are throwing 'EAI_AGAIN' and NXDOMAIN errors when resolving internal service endpoint payment-gateway.internal.corp. Direct IP pings to the pods succeed, but host lookups fail intermittently.
resolution: The team investigated CoreDNS metrics in Prometheus and identified severe UDP packet drop on port 53 across worker nodes. Running 'kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns' showed upstream rate-limiting errors from the datacenter Bind9 DNS forwarder. The issue was mitigated by auto-scaling CoreDNS replicas from 2 to 8, configuring the CoreDNS cache plugin with a 30-second TTL minimum, and tuning upstream resolver UDP buffer sizes with 'sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=26214400'.
ground_truth: The root cause was CoreDNS upstream forwarder rate-limiting due to UDP port exhaustion on the primary internal resolver node. Resolved by auto-scaling CoreDNS replicas, configuring CoreDNS cache plugin with a 30-second TTL minimum, and directing upstream queries to redundant internal DNS servers.

short_description: VPN disconnecting every 15 minutes
description: Remote employees connecting through GlobalProtect VPN get forcibly disconnected every 15 to 20 minutes and have to re-authenticate repeatedly.
resolution: Diagnostics inspected the Palo Alto GlobalProtect gateway system logs. The audit revealed a conflicting Dead Peer Detection (DPD) timeout set to 15 seconds alongside an overly aggressive Inactivity Logout Timer of 900 seconds in the client gateway configuration. The network engineer updated the GlobalProtect gateway profile to extend the session inactivity timeout to 8 hours, adjusted the DPD interval to 60 seconds, and committed the changes. Client connection telemetry verified zero involuntary disconnects over a 4-hour window.
ground_truth: The root cause was an idle-timeout policy collision in the GlobalProtect gateway profile combined with an aggressive Dead Peer Detection (DPD) interval. Resolved by setting the GlobalProtect session timeout to 8 hours, increasing the DPD timeout to 60 seconds on the firewall, and deploying updated configs.

short_description: SSL Handshake Failure on Ingress Gateway for Merchant Onboarding API
description: External merchant systems attempting to upload batch registration data via https://api.merchant-onboard.com are receiving SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL and TLS handshake timeout errors. F5 BIG-IP load balancer shows a spike in unfinished client handshakes.
resolution: The team ran 'openssl s_client -connect api.merchant-onboard.com:443 -servername api.merchant-onboard.com -showcerts' and discovered that the SSL Client Profile on the F5 BIG-IP was missing the intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) chain file. Additionally, client hello packets requesting TLS 1.3 were dropping due to an incompatible elliptic curve cipher suite list. The engineer uploaded the complete DigiCert CA bundle, enabled standard ECDHE ciphers in the SSL Client Profile, and tested handshake completion with curl and Postman.
ground_truth: The root cause was an incomplete intermediate CA certificate chain on the Ingress VIP SSL Client Profile and an unoptimized TLS 1.3 cipher suite negotiation. Resolved by bundling the DigiCert Intermediate CA with the server certificate on the F5 profile, updating cipher suites, and verifying handshake completion.

short_description: Slow internet and dropped calls in Building B 3rd Floor
description: Multiple users on the 3rd floor of Building B complain that Microsoft Teams calls are robotic, breaking up, and dropping every few minutes. Speedtest shows high jitter.
resolution: Wireless site survey utilizing Aruba AirWave identified severe co-channel interference on 5GHz Channel 36 and Channel 44 across access points AP-3B-01 and AP-3B-02, with channel utilization exceeding 82%. A rogue non-corporate wireless bridge was also flooding 2.4GHz spectrum. The network team enabled Dynamic Channel Assignment (DCA) with 40MHz channel width, reduced AP transmit power from 18dBm to 12dBm to eliminate cell overlap, and relocated the rogue bridge. Post-change spectrum analysis showed channel utilization below 22% with jitter dropping to <5ms.
ground_truth: The root cause was severe co-channel Wi-Fi interference on 5GHz channels caused by overlapping access point radio coverage and high channel saturation. Resolved by enabling Dynamic Channel Allocation (DCA) on the wireless controller, reducing AP transmit power, and optimizing 5GHz channel distribution.

short_description: Outbound Webhook Delivery Blocked by Perimeter Firewall Rule
description: Automated webhook events notifying partner banking networks of completed transactions are failing with connection timeout (SYN_SENT without SYN-ACK). Internal queue is backing up past 15,000 unacknowledged messages.
resolution: Engineers executed 'diag sniffer packet any "host 198.51.100.25 and port 8443" 4' on the perimeter Fortinet firewall and observed outbound TCP SYN packets being dropped by default deny rule 0. Cross-referencing change tickets revealed that a recent security policy push omitted the newly onboarded partner bank IP block. The network team created an explicit outbound egress policy rule permitting TCP 8443 to CIDR 198.51.100.0/24 with source NAT enabled. The webhook dispatcher instantly re-established connections and drained the queue within 12 minutes.
ground_truth: The root cause was a recent perimeter firewall policy push that omitted the partner bank's new CIDR block from the outbound egress rules, causing TCP SYN timeouts. Resolved by adding the CIDR range to the egress firewall whitelist, re-establishing sessions, and draining the webhook queue.

short_description: Switch stack offline in Distribution Center 4
description: Core access switch stack in DC-4 warehouse went unreachable at 03:00. Warehouse barcode scanners and shipping label printers cannot connect to the LAN.
resolution: Console access into Cisco Catalyst 9300 switch stack via out-of-band terminal server revealed a stack split-brain condition caused by a physically degraded StackWise-480 flex cable between Switch Member 1 and Member 2. The loopback test confirmed CRC errors on Stack Port 2. An on-call technician replaced the damaged StackWise cable and rebooted Member 2. The stack re-elected Member 1 as Master, synchronized running configurations, and restored all 96 PoE ports for scanners and printers.
ground_truth: The root cause was a stack split caused by a faulty StackWise flex-cable between switch stack members, leading to election failure and port isolation. Resolved by replacing the damaged StackWise cable, restoring stack synchronization, and recovering all warehouse access ports.

short_description: DHCP Pool Exhaustion in Guest Wi-Fi and Staging VLAN
description: Newly provisioned merchant POS demo units in the staging lab are failing to obtain IP addresses, displaying 169.254.x.x APIPA addresses. DHCP server logs indicate no available leases in Scope 10.45.20.0/24.
resolution: Inspection of the Infoblox DDI appliance confirmed that the DHCP scope for VLAN 20 (10.45.20.0/24) was 100% utilized due to a default 7-day lease time applied to high-turnover testing terminals. The network engineer resized the subnet mask from /24 to /23 (expanding the range to 10.45.20.0/23), reduced the DHCP lease duration to 4 hours, and flushed inactive stale leases with 'clearpool'. POS devices immediately received valid IP configurations via DHCP Discover/Ack.
ground_truth: The root cause was an unreleased 7-day DHCP lease duration on VLAN 20 which exhausted all available IP leases due to rapid test device turnover. Resolved by expanding the DHCP scope subnet from /24 to /23, reducing the lease duration to 4 hours, and clearing expired leases.

short_description: Large File Data Sync Fails Over MPLS Due to Path MTU Black Hole
description: Database backup replication between Dallas DC and Chicago DR site stalls indefinitely whenever packet payloads exceed 1460 bytes. Small ICMP pings succeed, but large rsync transfers freeze at 0% after initial handshake.
resolution: Diagnostics executed 'ping -s 1472 -M do 10.100.50.12' which returned 'Frag needed and DF set' without ICMP Type 3 Code 4 replies reaching the sender due to an upstream ISP filtering ICMP unreachables. The network team implemented TCP MSS clamping on the WAN MPLS interfaces of edge routers rtr-dal-01 and rtr-chi-01 using 'ip tcp adjust-mss 1360'. Testing with large file transfers over rsync and MySQL replication confirmed continuous high-speed data flow without stalling.
ground_truth: The root cause was ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) packets being dropped by transit routers, causing Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD) to fail over the MPLS link. Resolved by configuring 'ip tcp adjust-mss 1360' on MPLS WAN interfaces on both endpoint routers.

short_description: Sales Manager Missing Elevated Approver Permissions in CRM Module
description: Newly promoted Regional Sales Manager cannot approve merchant fee waivers exceeding $5,000 in Salesforce/CRM. System throws 'Permission Denied: Insufficient Privileges to Execute Action' upon clicking Approve.
resolution: IT Support investigated the user's role assignments in Okta and Salesforce. The audit revealed that while the user's job title was updated in HR Workday, the Okta SAML claims group mapping had not pushed the 'CRM_Tier2_Approver' permission set to Salesforce. The technician added the user to Active Directory security group 'SG_CRM_Tier2_Approvers', initiated an Okta SCIM sync, and assigned the 'Fee Waiver Escalation Authority' permission set in Salesforce Setup. The user successfully approved pending fee waiver requests.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the user's Okta SAML claims group mapping was not synchronized with the CRM 'Tier-2 Approver' permission set following their promotion. Resolved by updating the user's Active Directory security group membership, triggering an Okta SCIM directory sync, and verifying the approval workflow.

short_description: Screen goes white when signing agreement
description: Merchant called in stating that whenever they click the final submit button on the e-signature tablet, the whole page turns blank white and nothing happens. No confirmation email is received.
resolution: Support engineer checked the browser console and client telemetry on the merchant's Samsung Galaxy Tab A8. The logs revealed an Uncaught TypeError in the client-side JavaScript bundle caused by stale cached DOM elements colliding with an updated CSRF token validation script. The technician instructed the merchant to clear the browser storage and site data in Chrome settings, pushed the updated merchant e-sign Web App bundle v2.4.1, and verified successful agreement submission and instant confirmation email generation.
ground_truth: The root cause was a corrupt local browser cache and localStorage state on the merchant tablet's WebView app colliding with a new CSRF token validation script. Resolved by clearing browser cache/storage, updating the web application bundle, and regenerating a fresh e-signature session token.

short_description: Repeated Active Directory Account Lockout for POS Provisioning Service Account
description: The dedicated service account svc-pos-provision gets locked out in Active Directory every 30 minutes, halting automated terminal configuration for newly registered retail merchants.
resolution: IT Support analyzed Windows Security Event logs on Primary Domain Controller DC-01. Filtering for Event ID 4740 (Account Lockout) identified caller machine 'STG-APP-04'. Remote inspection of STG-APP-04 revealed an old scheduled background task running a deprecated provisioning script with stale cached service account credentials. The technician disabled the orphaned task, updated the Windows Credential Manager store with the current password, and unlocked the account in Active Directory. Lockout monitoring confirmed zero subsequent events.
ground_truth: The root cause was a decommissioned staging server that still had a scheduled task running with cached, expired credentials for svc-pos-provision, causing repeated bad password attempts against the Domain Controller. Resolved by locating the source workstation via Event ID 4740, disabling the orphaned scheduled task, and unlocking the account.

short_description: Can't login to merchant dashboard after password reset
description: User reset password via self-service portal, received confirmation email, but when attempting to log in, the dashboard displays 'Invalid credentials or session expired' error.
resolution: IT Support examined Keycloak authentication logs and Active Directory replication health. The self-service portal had written the new password hash to DC-01, but inter-site replication to DC-02 (used by the web frontend auth pool) was delayed due to an RPC replication backlog. The technician ran 'repadmin /syncall /AePdq' to force immediate directory replication across all domain controllers and revoked all active OAuth refresh tokens for the user account. The user subsequently authenticated successfully.
ground_truth: The root cause was replication latency between Active Directory Domain Controllers combined with a cached Kerberos ticket on the web frontend. Resolved by manually triggering AD inter-site replication via repadmin, revoking active session tokens, and verifying login authentication.

short_description: YubiKey FIDO2 Hardware Token Not Recognized on macOS Workstations
description: Support engineers running macOS Sonoma are unable to complete multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the internal incident ticketing portal using YubiKey 5C NFC hardware tokens. Chrome browser reports 'The operation timed out or was not allowed by the user'.
resolution: Investigation indicated that the recently pushed macOS Sonoma security update revoked default USB smart card daemon (pcscd) access for non-admin user contexts. IT Support packaged and deployed an updated Jamf configuration profile enabling the SmartCard and FIDO2 entitlements under /Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins. Additionally, Chrome enterprise policy was updated to explicitly allow WebAuthn USB device access for the ticketing portal domain. Hardware token authentication completed successfully on test Macs.
ground_truth: The root cause was an outdated WebAuthn / FIDO2 middleware profile on macOS clients and missing USB entitlement permissions in the Chrome enterprise policy. Resolved by deploying the updated YubiKey CCID configuration profile via Jamf Pro MDM and updating the Chrome enterprise policy.

short_description: Payment terminal receipt printer not printing receipts
description: POS terminal at register 3 completes credit card transactions successfully, but the thermal receipt printer does not output any paper and makes a beeping noise.
resolution: Support technician remotely connected to the POS station and inspected the Windows Print Spooler service (`spoolsv.exe`). The print queue contained a corrupted 0-byte print job that stalled the spooler thread. The technician stopped the Print Spooler service via PowerShell `Stop-Service Spooler`, deleted all orphaned `.SPL` and `.SHD` files in `C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS`, re-aligned the Epson TM-T88VI COM3 port baud rate to 19200 bps in Device Manager, and restarted the spooler service. Test receipt printed immediately.
ground_truth: The root cause was a stalled Windows Print Spooler service caused by a corrupted raw print job in the spool directory coupled with a misconfigured serial baud rate on the thermal printer. Resolved by stopping the spooler, clearing orphaned print files, matching the COM port baud rate, and testing print output.

short_description: Automated Onboarding Welcome Emails Bouncing with 554 Relay Access Denied
description: New merchants are not receiving their onboarding activation emails. The notification service log shows SMTP delivery failure: '554 5.7.1 <dest@domain.com>: Relay access denied' when communicating with the corporate Exchange relay.
resolution: IT Support checked Exchange Server connector logs. An automated infrastructure scaling event had deployed new application worker nodes under IP subnet 10.244.18.0/24, which was missing from the Microsoft Exchange Receive Connector's trusted internal IP whitelist. The administrator added the new worker subnet using PowerShell `Set-ReceiveConnector "Internal Relay App" -RemoteIPRanges (Get-ReceiveConnector "Internal Relay App").RemoteIPRanges + "10.244.18.0/24"`. The mail dispatcher was restarted, and 148 queued welcome emails were successfully delivered.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the outbound IP address of the newly scaled onboarding worker node was not added to the Microsoft Exchange Server Receive Connector anonymous relay whitelist. Resolved by registering the new worker pod subnet in Exchange Receive Connector settings and restarting the mail dispatcher queue.

short_description: Merchant Agreement PDF download generates corrupted 0-byte file
description: When agents click 'Download Executed Agreement' in the Merchant Management portal, the generated PDF downloads as a 0-byte corrupted file that cannot be opened.
resolution: Diagnostics checked the PDF rendering container pod logs (`kubectl logs -l app=pdf-generator`). The logs revealed 'ENOSPC: no space left on device' when writing temporary HTML render buffers to `/tmp/render`. The ephemeral storage volume had filled with un-cleared wkhtmltopdf raster cache files. The support engineer cleared the `/tmp` directory, expanded the pod ephemeral storage request to 4Gi in the Helm deployment values, and added an hourly cron cleanup script. PDF generation was verified on 10 random merchant accounts.
ground_truth: The root cause was temporary disk space exhaustion in `/tmp` on the rendering service container, preventing the PDF generator from writing the converted file before streaming. Resolved by purging temporary files, increasing container ephemeral storage limits, and adding automated cache cleanup.

short_description: OAuth2 Token Scope Mismatch Blocking Mobile App Fee Calculator
description: Field sales agents using the mobile onboarding application receive '401 Unauthorized: Scope Insufficient' when invoking the /api/v2/pricing/calculate-fee endpoint after the latest app release.
resolution: IT Support analyzed the API Gateway access logs and Keycloak client definitions. Following the deployment of Fee Calculation API v2.2, the endpoint required the new 'fees:calculate' OAuth2 scope. However, the 'mobile_sales_app' Keycloak client was only configured with 'fees:read'. The technician updated the client scope mappings in Keycloak administration console, added 'fees:calculate' as a default client scope, and refreshed the mobile application session. Sales agents confirmed fee calculations were functioning normally.
ground_truth: The root cause was a missing 'fees:calculate' scope in the Mobile Client OAuth2 App registration within Keycloak following the API gateway upgrade. Resolved by adding the required scopes to the mobile client definition in Keycloak and issuing a token refresh to active sessions.

short_description: Cannot change merchant bank account routing number in portal
description: Customer service rep reports that the input field for 'Bank Routing Transit Number (ABA)' is completely greyed out and uneditable for existing merchants requesting a bank detail update.
resolution: IT Support reviewed the CRM merchant record state and UI permission rules. The routing number field was disabled by design because the merchant account was currently flagged in 'Audit Hold' status due to an unverified tax ID update. The representative was guided to execute the required 'Bank Account Change Request' approval flow in the CRM, which dispatches a verification link to the merchant's authorized signer and unlocks the banking form once manager approval is recorded. Form fields became editable as expected.
ground_truth: The root cause was a conditional UI field-lock triggered because the merchant record was in 'Audit Hold' status, requiring an approved Change Request workflow before inline banking edits are permitted. Resolved by guiding the representative to initiate the standard Change Request approval workflow.

short_description: OSPF Adjacency Stuck in ExStart on Core Distribution Link
description: After a scheduled firmware upgrade on core switch sw-dist-01, OSPF neighbor relationship with sw-core-02 is stuck in ExStart/Exchange state over VLAN 99. Routing tables are not exchanging, resulting in sub-optimal traffic routing through backup 1G link.
resolution: The network engineer examined OSPF packet debugs with 'debug ip ospf adj' on sw-dist-01, which revealed that Database Description (DBD) packets were being repeatedly dropped due to an MTU mismatch. Sw-dist-01 was configured for 9000-byte jumbo frames, while sw-core-02 reverted to default 1500-byte MTU after the firmware reboot. The team standardized the MTU to 9000 bytes on sw-core-02 interface TenGigE1/0/2 with 'mtu 9000' and 'ip ospf mtu-ignore' verification. OSPF state immediately transitioned to Full and optimal routing was restored.
ground_truth: The root cause was an MTU mismatch on the trunk sub-interface (sw-dist-01 was set to 9000 bytes jumbo frames while sw-core-02 reverted to default 1500 bytes after firmware reboot), preventing DBD packet exchange. Resolved by standardizing MTU to 9000 across both interfaces with 'mtu 9000' and verifying OSPF Full adjacency.

short_description: Can't access branch server from office desk
description: An account manager reports that their desktop computer cannot open the shared folder or web admin page on the Austin branch server since this morning. It says network path not found.
resolution: Diagnostics traced network routing between the headquarters subnet (10.10.30.0/24) and Austin branch subnet (10.30.50.0/24). Inspection of aggregation switch sw-agg-03 revealed that a recent maintenance script accidentally pruned VLAN 110 (Branch Management) from the 802.1Q trunk allowed list. The technician added VLAN 110 back to trunk port-channel 2 using 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 110' and verified successful ICMP ping and SMB file share connectivity.
ground_truth: The root cause was an accidental VLAN pruning configuration change on intermediate aggregation switch sw-agg-03 that removed VLAN 110 (Branch Management) from the 802.1Q trunk allowed list. Resolved by adding VLAN 110 back to the trunk interface with 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 110' and validating reachability.

short_description: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway on Payment Webhook Ingestion During Flash Sale
description: During peak promotional traffic, external payment gateway webhooks from Stripe and Adyen are receiving HTTP 502 Bad Gateway responses from edge Nginx reverse proxy gw-ext.prod.corp. Upstream microservices show healthy CPU and memory.
resolution: Engineers reviewed Nginx error logs on edge gateway proxies (`/var/log/nginx/error.log`), which revealed thousands of 'upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream' and 'worker_connections are not enough' errors. The large JSON headers in the incoming webhooks overwhelmed the default 4k proxy buffer. The team increased proxy buffer parameters to 'proxy_buffer_size 128k; proxy_buffers 4 256k;' in the Nginx server block and bumped 'worker_rlimit_nofile 65535'. After executing 'nginx -s reload', 502 error rates dropped to zero.
ground_truth: The root cause was Nginx proxy buffer exhaustion caused by large JSON payload headers exceeding default buffer sizes and hitting max open file descriptor limits during high traffic. Resolved by tuning Nginx configuration with 'proxy_buffer_size 128k', 'proxy_buffers 4 256k', increasing worker connections, and reloading Nginx.

short_description: Zoom calls freeze when moving between conference rooms
description: Laptops lose connection for 30 to 45 seconds and video calls completely freeze when employees walk between Conference Room A and B on the 2nd floor.
resolution: Wireless capture telemetry on Cisco Wireless LAN Controller (WLC 9800) indicated that roaming clients were triggering full 802.1X EAP authentication on every AP handoff because Fast BSS Transition (802.11r) was disabled in the corporate WLAN profile. The network engineer enabled 802.11r Over-the-Air FT Roaming and 802.11v BSS Transition Management on the SSID profile. Roaming packet tests confirmed seamless client AP transitions in under 18ms with zero packet loss or video freeze.
ground_truth: The root cause was 802.11k/r Fast BSS Transition (FT) roaming being disabled on the corporate SSID profile, forcing full 802.1X EAP re-authentication upon every AP handoff. Resolved by enabling 802.11r Fast Roaming and 802.11v Assisted Roaming on the Cisco Wireless LAN Controller profile.

short_description: GRE Tunnel Down Between Primary Datacenter and AWS DirectConnect
description: Monitoring alerted that GRE tunnel interface tun101 connecting on-prem DC to AWS VPC transit gateway went into line protocol down state. Cloud database replication traffic is failing over to degraded public VPN.
resolution: Network engineers investigated border router rtr-border-01 and verified that the physical DirectConnect circuit was operational. However, 'show ip interface brief' showed Tunnel101 down due to keepalive failure. A firewall audit revealed that a recent automated security patch applied a transit ACL rule that accidentally denied IP protocol 47 (GRE). The team updated the ACL with 'permit gre host 198.19.10.1 host 198.19.20.1', cleared interface tunnel counters, and verified tunnel line protocol returned to UP/UP with sub-2ms latency.
ground_truth: The root cause was a transit ACL update on the upstream border router that blocked IP protocol 47 (GRE) and ICMP keepalive packets from the AWS DirectConnect gateway IP. Resolved by updating the edge ACL to permit IP protocol 47 bidirectionally between endpoints and resetting tunnel interfaces.

short_description: Everything is super slow in London office
description: London branch office manager submitted a ticket saying the entire office network feels sluggish today. Files take forever to save to the shared drive and web pages take 20 seconds to load.
resolution: Network Ops monitored traffic flows on the London branch Meraki MX edge appliance using NetFlow analysis. The dashboard showed that the 100Mbps DIA Internet circuit was running at 99.4% saturation caused by a workstation (LON-DESK-104) uploading a massive uncompressed 450GB raw database archive to an external cloud bucket. The engineer applied an immediate traffic shaping policy limiting workstation background upload throughput to 5Mbps and called the user to reschedule the backup during off-peak hours. Branch latency returned to 14ms.
ground_truth: The root cause was an unthrottled backup synchronization job running on workstation LON-DESK-104 during business hours, saturating 98% of the 100Mbps branch WAN uplink bandwidth. Resolved by applying a traffic-shaping Quality of Service (QoS) policy on the branch gateway router restricting background upload bandwidth.

short_description: STP Topology Change Storm Causing Network Micro-Loops in Datacenter Rack 7
description: High CPU utilization (99%) reported on Cisco Nexus 9300 leaf switches in Rack 7. Server NICs report massive broadcast storm packet counters and packet drops across all access ports in VLAN 40.
resolution: Log analysis via 'show logging' on leaf switch n9k-leaf-07 showed continuous 'STP-2-DISPUTE_DETECTED' and Topology Change Notifications (TCNs) received on port Eth1/24. Physical inspection revealed that a developer connected an unmanaged 8-port desk switch with loopback wiring into access port Eth1/24. The engineer enabled 'spanning-tree bpduguard enable' and 'spanning-tree portfast' on all access interfaces, which immediately err-disabled the offending port. Broadcast storm counters dropped to 0 and switch CPU returned to 6%.
ground_truth: The root cause was an unmanaged test switch plugged into access port Eth1/24 with Spanning Tree BPDU Guard disabled, triggering continuous Topology Change Notification (TCN) floods and packet loops. Resolved by enabling 'spanning-tree bpduguard enable' on all edge access ports and shutting down the offending port.

short_description: Cannot SSH into staging database cluster
description: DevOps engineers cannot connect to any staging database hosts via SSH on port 22. Connection times out with 'Operation timed out'.
resolution: Network Ops verified AWS VPC Security Group rules attached to staging database subnet sub-db-stg-01. A Terraform CI/CD pipeline run had overwritten the Ingress rule for TCP port 22, accidentally replacing the DevOps VPN CIDR block (10.80.0.0/16) with an empty list. The engineer reverted the Terraform state, re-applied the security group rule permitting SSH from the authorized VPN CIDR, and verified immediate terminal login access.
ground_truth: The root cause was an automated security group synchronization script that accidentally stripped the DevOps VPN CIDR (10.80.0.0/16) from the staging database subnet Ingress Security Group rules. Resolved by restoring the authorized CIDR in AWS Security Group rules and locking the Terraform state configuration.

short_description: Source NAT Port Exhaustion for Outbound Payment Gateway API Calls
description: Microservices running in private subnets are intermittently throwing 'Cannot assign requested address' (EADDRNOTAVAIL) when initiating outbound HTTPS transactions to third-party payment processors.
resolution: CloudWatch metrics for the NAT Gateway showed that `ErrorPortAllocation` metrics spiked during high volume spikes, indicating all 55,000 ephemeral source ports per allocated Elastic IP were exhausted. The team associated two secondary Elastic IPs to the NAT Gateway pool, expanding available concurrent ephemeral port capacity to 165,000. Additionally, application teams updated their HTTP clients to enable persistent TCP Keep-Alive connection reuse, eliminating port turnover.
ground_truth: The root cause was SNAT port exhaustion on the NAT Gateway pool because thousands of concurrent microservice HTTP requests were opening short-lived connections without TCP connection reuse. Resolved by allocating additional Elastic IPs to the NAT Gateway pool and configuring application HTTP clients with persistent connection pooling.

short_description: Inter-VNI VXLAN Traffic Dropping Between App and Database Tier
description: Application containers in Tenant VNI 50010 cannot communicate with database nodes in Tenant VNI 50020 across the Spine-Leaf fabric. Leaf switch leaf-01 ARP table shows incomplete MAC entries for remote VTEP.
resolution: BGP EVPN control plane inspection on leaf switch leaf-01 via 'show bgp l2vpn evpn vni 50020' showed that Type-5 IP Prefix routes were missing because the Symmetric IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) L3 VNI route-target was misconfigured as '65000:50010' instead of '65000:50020'. The engineer corrected the VRF Route Target export configuration under VRF 'PROD-DB' across all leaf switches and executed 'clear bgp l2vpn evpn * soft'. Inter-VNI routing latency dropped to <1ms.
ground_truth: The root cause was a missing Symmetric IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) L3 VNI route-target export configuration on leaf switch leaf-01 for VRF PROD-DB. Resolved by configuring matching BGP EVPN Route Distinguisher and Route Target 65000:50020 on all leaf switches and validating EVPN routes.

short_description: Kerberos Authentication Failure on Internal Reporting Portal
description: Finance users accessing https://reports.internal.corp receive HTTP 401.1 Unauthorized errors with Kerberos token error 'KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED'. NTLM fallback is disabled by security policy.
resolution: IT Support ran 'setspn -X' in Active Directory to search for duplicate Service Principal Names. The query identified that 'HTTP/reports.internal.corp' was registered both on service account 'svc-reports' and on a decommissioned host account 'REPORTS-SRV-OLD', causing ticket decryption mismatch. The technician deleted the duplicate SPN with 'setspn -D HTTP/reports.internal.corp REPORTS-SRV-OLD', issued 'klist purge' on client PCs, and verified seamless single sign-on authentication.
ground_truth: The root cause was a duplicate Service Principal Name (SPN) HTTP/reports.internal.corp registered against both service account svc-reports and old machine account REPORTS-SRV-OLD in Active Directory. Resolved by detecting duplicates with 'setspn -X', deleting the stale SPN, and purging client Kerberos tickets.

short_description: Outlook search bar not finding any recent emails
description: Executive assistant reports that searching for client names or invoice numbers in Outlook desktop returns zero results or says 'Search results may be incomplete' since yesterday's update.
resolution: Support technician remotely inspected the user's Windows Search service (`WSearch`) in services.msc and found the search index database file `C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Search\Data\Applications\Windows\Windows.edb` corrupted after an unexpected power outage. The technician stopped WSearch, opened Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild, and enabled Outlook data files under indexed locations. After indexing completed (15,200 items), Outlook search returned all recent and historical messages instantly.
ground_truth: The root cause was a corrupted Windows Search Index database (Windows.edb) following an abrupt system shutdown, preventing Outlook from querying local email caches. Resolved by rebuilding the Windows Indexing Options catalog, restarting the WSearch service, and verifying instant search retrieval.

short_description: Laptop Prompting for BitLocker Recovery Key on Every Boot
description: Field sales representative's Lenovo ThinkPad laptop prompts for a 48-digit BitLocker recovery key at every system reboot after receiving a BIOS firmware update from Lenovo Vantage.
resolution: Support engineer verified that the recent BIOS update modified the TPM PCR 7/11 measurement profile. The technician retrieved the user's 48-digit recovery key from Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), suspended BitLocker encryption in PowerShell using 'manage-bde -protectors -disable C: -rebootcount 1', rebooted the machine to allow TPM 2.0 to reseal the new platform configuration hash, and re-enabled protection with 'manage-bde -protectors -enable C:'. Subsequent restarts booted directly into Windows without recovery prompts.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the BIOS update modified the TPM PCR validation profile, causing TPM 2.0 to fail platform integrity measurements during boot. Resolved by retrieving the BitLocker recovery key from Microsoft Entra ID, suspending BitLocker for one reboot cycle via 'manage-bde', and re-enabling BitLocker to reseal the TPM state.

short_description: Dual monitor setup only mirroring display
description: User plugged in second Dell monitor via USB-C docking station, but Windows only allows 'Duplicate Display' and cannot detect the second screen as an extended display.
resolution: IT Support connected via remote assistance and inspected Device Manager under Display Adapters. The system was running Microsoft Basic Display Adapter driver due to a failed Intel graphics driver update. The technician downloaded and installed the certified Intel Iris Xe Graphics package and DisplayLink USB Graphics Software v11.1, restarted the laptop, and configured Display Settings with 'Extend these displays' at 2560x1440 resolution on both monitors.
ground_truth: The root cause was an outdated DisplayLink / Intel Graphics driver package that defaulted to fallback VGA mirroring over the DisplayPort-over-USB-C hub. Resolved by updating the DisplayLink docking station driver and Intel Iris Xe Graphics driver, and configuring Display Settings to 'Extend these displays'.

short_description: SAML SSO Assertion Expired Error on Salesforce Login
description: Users logging into Salesforce CRM via enterprise Okta SSO get blocked with error: 'Response contains an expired assertion. IssueInstant was too far in the past'.
resolution: IT Support investigated the Okta Active Directory agent server and discovered that the Windows Time Service (w32time) had failed to synchronize with the external NTP pool, resulting in a 145-second clock drift ahead of UTC. Because Salesforce enforces a strict 120-second clock skew threshold, the SAML Response timestamp was rejected. The administrator forced NTP clock resynchronization with 'w32tm /resync /force' and adjusted the SAML Assertion Clock Skew tolerance to 300 seconds in Salesforce Setup. SSO logins functioned immediately.
ground_truth: The root cause was an NTP time drift of 145 seconds on the primary identity server, exceeding Salesforce SAML maximum clock skew tolerance of 120 seconds. Resolved by resynchronizing the identity server NTP client with 'w32tm /resync /force' against NTP pool and setting clock-skew allowance to 300 seconds.

short_description: Cannot submit expense report button is missing
description: Employee trying to submit monthly travel expense report says the orange 'Submit for Approval' button is completely gone from the Concur portal interface.
resolution: Support technician reviewed the employee's user record in the ERP/Concur management console. The user was transferred to the Enterprise Sales division last week, but the HR Workday-to-Concur provisioning sync failed to populate the new 'Department Cost Center' code (CC-5020). Without an active cost center, the expense workflow cannot determine the approval manager hierarchy and suppresses the submit button. The technician manually assigned Cost Center CC-5020 and triggered profile sync. The submit button appeared and the report was dispatched.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the user's default cost center ID in the employee profile was unassigned during an internal department transfer, violating the mandatory routing policy requirement before submission. Resolved by assigning Department Cost Center code CC-5020 to the user profile and resyncing permissions.

short_description: Mobile Email Access Blocked Due to Device Non-Compliance in Microsoft Intune
description: VP of Sales cannot access work emails or Teams on iPhone. The Microsoft Authenticator app displays 'Your device is not compliant with company security policies'.
resolution: IT Support reviewed the device status in Microsoft Intune Endpoint Manager admin center. The user's corporate-managed iPhone was running iOS 16.5, which fell below the newly mandated Intune compliance baseline requiring iOS 17.2 or higher for mobile device management (MDM). The technician guided the user to connect to Wi-Fi and update iOS under Settings > General > Software Update, and then initiated an immediate device compliance check in the Microsoft Company Portal app. Conditional Access granted full access to Outlook and Teams upon verification.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the user's iOS version was running 16.5, falling below the updated Microsoft Intune Minimum OS Compliance Policy requirement of iOS 17.2, triggering an automated Conditional Access block. Resolved by updating iOS to the compliant release and forcing a compliance evaluation sync in Company Portal.

short_description: Badge reader not unlocking 4th floor IT server room
description: Lead systems engineer's physical RFID access badge is rejected with a double-red flash and beep at the 4th floor server room access door.
resolution: IT Support logged into the Lenel OnGuard Physical Access Control System (PACS) and queried badge number 84920. The access record showed that the engineer's annual privileged datacenter security clearance had reached its 365-day expiration date yesterday. After verifying manager authorization approval in ServiceNow ticket REQ09412, the technician extended the badge clearance validity for another 12 months and pushed the updated access badge profile to the 4th floor Lenel door controller panel. Badge reader unlocked on first tap.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the physical access badge credential in the Lenel OnGuard access control system had expired after its mandatory 12-month security clearance review cycle. Resolved by verifying active server room security authorization in ServiceNow, extending the badge expiration date by 12 months, and pushing updates to the door controller.

short_description: OneDrive for Business Sync Engine Stalled with Error 0x8004de40
description: Regional accounting team members cannot sync shared Excel financial spreadsheets. The OneDrive sync client displays 'Syncing 1 of 1,240 files' continuously and throws error code 0x8004de40.
resolution: IT Support remoted into the affected user workstation and diagnosed the OneDrive sync engine. The local Office Document Cache in `%localappdata%\Microsoft\Office\16.0\OfficeFileCache` had deadlocked file handles following an abnormal system shutdown during co-authoring sync. The technician closed OneDrive, ran '%localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive\onedrive.exe /reset' via Windows Run dialog, cleared the temporary Office file cache folder, and restarted OneDrive. The sync engine performed a clean metadata reconciliation and synced all 1,240 files within 6 minutes.
ground_truth: The root cause was a locked Office Document Cache temporary database containing conflicting locked handles from an abrupt system shutdown during multi-user co-authoring. Resolved by running 'onedrive.exe /reset', purging the OfficeFileCache temporary directory, and restarting the sync client.

short_description: New hire laptop missing all company software
description: New employee started today in customer onboarding, received a Dell laptop out of the box, but the desktop is completely empty. No merchant portals, VPN, or company apps are installed.
resolution: IT Support inspected the device enrollment state in Microsoft Intune / Windows Autopilot. The newly registered device serial number was not added to the dynamic Entra ID Device Security Group 'SG-Autopilot-Onboarding-Apps', causing the Autopilot Enrollment Status Page (ESP) to skip mandatory Win32 app deployments (GlobalProtect VPN, Chrome, Merchant Sales Portal, CrowdStrike). The technician added the device to the security group and initiated a remote policy sync. Intune pushed and installed all 8 required corporate applications within 25 minutes.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the newly provisioned device had not been assigned to the Autopilot Device Security Group in Microsoft Intune, causing Autopilot application deployment to be skipped. Resolved by assigning the device serial number to the targeted device group in Intune, triggering a remote sync, and verifying automated software installation.

short_description: LACP Port-Channel Flapping and Intermittent Packet Drops on Core Switch
description: Monitoring reported intermittent 15-20% packet drops between distribution switch sw-dist-02 and core router rtr-core-01. Port-channel 10 shows member interface TenGigE0/1/1 flapping between 'Bundled' and 'Suspended' states every few minutes.
resolution: The network engineer checked LACP bundle telemetry using 'show lacp internal' and 'show interfaces TenGigE0/1/1 transceiver detail'. Diagnostics revealed an optical power degradation on the SFP+ transceiver (Tx power at -18.2 dBm) coupled with an LACP rate timer mismatch: sw-dist-02 was sending LACP fast packets (1-second heartbeat) while rtr-core-01 was set to default slow (30-second heartbeat), causing frequent protocol timeouts under load. The team replaced the degraded optical SFP+ module, configured 'lacp rate fast' on both ends of Port-Channel 10, and verified zero packet drops and consistent bundle convergence.
ground_truth: The root cause was an LACP rate timer mismatch (fast vs slow heartbeats) combined with an optically degraded SFP+ transceiver on interface TenGigE0/1/1 causing frequent member suspensions. Resolved by standardizing 'lacp rate fast' across both endpoints, replacing the optical module, and verifying stable bundle convergence.

short_description: Store POS terminals cannot process credit cards since 8 AM
description: Store manager at retail location 114 reports that all three checkout registers fail when swiping credit cards, displaying 'Gateway Communication Error - Host Unreachable'. Standard internet browsing on the manager's back-office PC is working.
resolution: Network Ops reviewed firewall traffic logs on the store's edge Cisco ISR 4331 router. Packet capture on interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0 showed outbound TCP SYN packets from POS terminals (10.114.20.0/24) to payment processor endpoint 198.51.100.40 on TCP port 9002 being blocked by an access-list applied during overnight automated security hardening. The engineer updated the store ACL to permit outbound TCP 9002 traffic to the authorized processor subnet, cleared translation sessions with 'clear ip nat translation *', and confirmed instantaneous credit card approvals on all registers.
ground_truth: The root cause was an outbound firewall policy on the store's edge router blocking TCP port 9002 used for encrypted payment gateway processing after an automated security ACL push. Resolved by adding an outbound permit rule for TCP port 9002 to the payment processing endpoint on the store router and verifying successful transaction authorizations.

short_description: Anycast DNS Node Dropping Out of BGP Routing Table in Dallas POP
description: Global traffic routing telemetry shows 100% of DNS resolution traffic from the central region failing over to the Chicago datacenter. Dallas POP Anycast DNS node dns-dal-01 is operational locally, but BGP route injection for 192.0.2.53/32 has stopped.
resolution: Engineers connected to dns-dal-01 and examined the BIRD BGP routing daemon logs (`/var/log/bird.log`). The local health-checker script had stopped announcing the /32 host route to upstream Arista spine switches because a deadlocked socket in BIND/named was failing local UDP health queries (`dig @127.0.0.1 healthcheck.internal`). The team restarted the named DNS service, tuned the BIRD health-check timeout from 2s to 5s to prevent false-positive route withdrawals during query spikes, and verified that Dallas POP BGP route announcements were restored globally.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the BIRD BGP route daemon health-check script on dns-dal-01 failed due to a locked named query socket, causing it to withdraw the BGP host route advertisement from upstream spine routers. Resolved by restarting the named DNS service, tuning the health-check timeout, and restoring BGP route announcements.

short_description: Guest Wi-Fi captive portal not popping up on smartphones
description: Visitors in the main lobby connect to 'Corporate-Guest' Wi-Fi, but the browser login page never opens and devices show 'No Internet Connection'.
resolution: Wireless engineers captured traffic on the Cisco 9800 Wireless LAN Controller for guest clients on VLAN 50. The analysis revealed that the pre-authentication redirect ACL was blocking UDP port 53 to external DNS servers and dropping HTTP probing requests to Apple and Google captive network assistant URLs (`captive.apple.com` and `connectivitycheck.gstatic.com`). The engineer modified the pre-auth ACL to permit UDP 53 to internal DNS forwarders and allowed clear HTTP port 80 redirection to the Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) guest portal web server. Captive portal redirect popped up immediately on iOS and Android test devices.
ground_truth: The root cause was that HTTP/HTTPS redirection rules in the Cisco WLC pre-authentication ACL were dropping initial DNS interception queries for captive portal detection domains. Resolved by updating the pre-auth ACL on the WLC to permit DNS (UDP 53) and allow clear HTTP redirection to the guest portal server.

short_description: IPsec Site-to-Site VPN Tunnel Rekeying Failure with Third-Party Warehouse
description: Site-to-site VPN tunnel vpn-3pl-logistics drops every 8 hours exactly. Initial tunnel establishment succeeds, but Phase 2 Quick Mode rekeying negotiations fail with 'QM FSM error: NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN'.
resolution: Network Ops inspected Cisco ASA firewall crypto debug logs with 'debug crypto ipsec 255'. The logs revealed that during the 28,800-second Phase 2 rekey, the local ASA requested Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) with Diffie-Hellman Group 14, but the third-party Fortinet gateway rejected the proposal because it was configured for DH Group 19. The engineer updated the IPsec crypto map on the ASA with 'set pfs group19' to synchronize Diffie-Hellman parameters. Automated rekey testing was monitored through three complete cycles with zero dropped packet connections.
ground_truth: The root cause was a Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) mismatch in the Phase 2 IPsec transform set: the local gateway requested DH Group 14 while the third-party warehouse firewall expected DH Group 19 during rekeying. Resolved by updating the Phase 2 crypto map on the ASA firewall to match DH Group 19 and verifying seamless automated rekeys.

short_description: LDAPS Over SSL Authentication Failure for Internal Web Portals
description: Internal web applications (Jira, Confluence, Merchant Admin) report 'LDAP Server Down / SSL Handshake Failed' when users attempt to log in using Active Directory credentials over port 636.
resolution: IT Support analyzed Event Viewer logs on Primary Domain Controller DC-01 under Directory-Services. Event ID 1220 indicated that the LDAPS server SSL certificate expired at 00:00 UTC. The technician generated a new 2-year Domain Controller Authentication certificate from the internal Microsoft Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) server, installed it in the Local Computer Personal Certificate store, and executed 'certutil -repairstore my <Thumbprint>' to bind the private key. After restarting Active Directory Domain Services (`NTDS`), LDAPS connectivity over port 636 was verified with `ldp.exe` and web portal logins were restored.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the server SSL/TLS certificate installed on Domain Controller DC-01 for LDAPS expired, causing client applications to abort TLS validation. Resolved by generating a new domain certificate from the internal Microsoft Enterprise Certificate Authority, binding it to the Active Directory service, and verifying port 636 connectivity.

short_description: Can't click on any links in corporate web portal
description: Operations agent states that inside the merchant servicing portal, clicking on buttons or links does nothing and the mouse cursor stays as a spinning wheel on Windows 11.
resolution: Support technician initiated a remote screen session and inspected Chrome Developer Tools (F12) on the user's computer. The console showed continuous Uncaught SecurityError exceptions caused by an unauthorized browser extension ('AdBlock Plus / Privacy Shield') that had injected a script intercepting all DOM click events on React components. The technician uninstalled the extension, configured Google Chrome Enterprise Policy in Google Workspace to block unapproved extensions, and cleared the user's browser cache. All portal buttons and navigation links became fully interactive.
ground_truth: The root cause was an unauthorized Chrome browser extension that injected an aggressive content script blocking internal DOM click events on the web portal. Resolved by disabling the rogue browser extension, enforcing an extension blocklist via Google Chrome Enterprise Policy, and clearing browser site data.

short_description: Network Shared Printer Installation Blocked with Error 0x0000011b
description: Finance department users cannot connect to the shared network laser printer on print server PRNT-SRV-01. Windows displays error: 'Operation failed with error 0x0000011b'.
resolution: IT Support investigated the print server logs. Following the deployment of Microsoft security patch KB5005565 addressing the PrintNightmare vulnerability, Windows enforced Point and Print RPC authentication encryption by default, causing un-hardened Windows clients to fail with error 0x0000011b. The technician deployed an updated Type 4 universal print driver package via Group Policy and added the registry key `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\RpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled = 0` on the print server. Client workstations immediately mapped the printer queue without errors.
ground_truth: The root cause was a recent Windows security patch enforcing Point and Print RPC encryption (RpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled) which rejected legacy client driver requests. Resolved by configuring print server registry keys, updating Type 4 universal print drivers via Group Policy, and mapping client printer queues.

short_description: Locked out of corporate laptop while traveling abroad
description: Senior director traveling in Japan entered password correctly but Windows says 'Your credentials could not be verified because your domain is not available'.
resolution: Support engineer assisted the executive over phone. The laptop's cached domain credentials had been purged following a local Windows BitLocker PIN reset, and the machine had no direct connectivity to on-prem Domain Controllers from the hotel Wi-Fi. The technician guided the user to click the 'Network Sign-in / GlobalProtect VPN' tile on the Windows 11 lock screen to establish a Start-Before-Logon (SBL) VPN connection using their MFA token. Once the VPN connected to the US gateway, the laptop authenticated against DC-01, refreshed its cached credentials, and allowed desktop login.
ground_truth: The root cause was that the laptop's cached domain credentials buffer was cleared during an offline system recovery, requiring direct line-of-sight to an Active Directory Domain Controller before local Windows logon is permitted. Resolved by establishing a Start-Before-Logon (SBL) GlobalProtect VPN tunnel directly from the Windows lock screen to authenticate against the Domain Controller.

short_description: Continuous Multi-Factor Authentication Prompt Loop on Microsoft 365 Apps
description: Corporate users on macOS and Windows are prompted for Microsoft Authenticator push approvals every 5 minutes in Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and OneDrive desktop apps without ever achieving a persistent session.
resolution: IT Support investigated Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Conditional Access audit logs. An administrator had recently updated a Conditional Access policy named 'M365-Global-Session-Control' and mistakenly set the 'Sign-in Frequency' control to 5 minutes instead of 8 hours, causing continuous Primary Refresh Token (PRT) invalidations. The administrator updated the policy to an 8-hour periodic re-authentication window with 'Persistent Browser Session' set to Always. Within 10 minutes of policy propagation, MFA authentication prompt loops stopped across all client endpoints.
ground_truth: The root cause was an administrator error in a Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access Policy that enforced an aggressive 'Sign-in Frequency' of 5 minutes instead of 8 hours, causing immediate Primary Refresh Token (PRT) invalidation across Office apps. Resolved by correcting the Session Control policy to an 8-hour window with persistent sessions enabled.
